newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cork rural results may be added to Dublin summit statement.
newsitem.headline: Cork rural results may be added to Dublin summit statement.

text.p: The Irish EU Presidency will seek to include some of the conclusions of the recent Cork rural development conference in next month's EU Dublin summit statement, Irish farm minister Ivan Yates said on Monday.
Asked about opposition from some countries, Yates told a news conference that ministers only held a preliminary discussion on Monday.

"People did not want to be jumped into major decisions by way of declarations. That wasn't the intention," he said. "We see this as the start of a process and member states will have the opportunity...to give more detailed comments."
Germany and the Netherlands had called for further discussions in the Farm Council while France and Spain stressed the need to safeguard the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), EU officials said.
But Britain, Sweden and Finland welcomed the Cork declaration's call for further significant farm reform.

The Cork declaration, issued at an EU conference on rural development from November 7-9, noted that the CAP "will have to adapt to new realities and challenges in terms of consumer demand and preferences, international trade developments, and the EU's next enlargement."
Yates said the Irish Presidency would like the Dublin summit to take note of the Cork declaration and annex it to the Dublin statement.
The issue will be discussed at the next General Affairs Council.
